lesson_title: The Rhino in the Glass Case
hook_text: A tiny golden rhino, buried for about eight hundred years. What can it tell us?
clip_script: Pretoria, a museum gallery. In a glass case: a small golden rhinoceros, made of thin gold foil pressed over a carved wooden body. It was found in 1933 in a royal grave on Mapungubwe Hill, in Limpopo. Mapungubwe was a kingdom about eight hundred years ago. Its people left no writing, so we learn from objects, buildings, bones and stories. This term in Grade 6 History: an African kingdom long ago.
visual_style: Whiteboard glass case with a golden rhino drawing itself, then a timeline from 900 to 1300 AD.
mood: Awed and curious, like opening a treasure chest from the past.
pacing: Slow reveal of the rhino, then a quick map of the four History topics, ending on the timeline.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find Mapungubwe on a map of Limpopo.
